name: Sailing
pages: Having launched your Craft and rigged it from Stem to Stern, few Obstacles stand between you and the open Sea. Yet pay Heed – a Ship, however finely wrought, is mere Drift-Wood without a capable Helmsman.  It remains for you to launch it into a suitable Harbor, and to study the Arts of Pilotry and Navigation.$(br)   When you are ready to set sail, board your Ship and take in the View from the Helm. Once accustomed to your new Environs, the Voyage may commence

With a firm Hand on the Tiller $(o)(A/D)$(), turn the Prow towards the open Sea and unfurl the Sails $(o)(R)$(). Presently they shall catch Wind and your Vessel is under Way. To gain Speed, trim the Sails $(o)(W)$(), setting them until the Sheets are taut. To slow, slacken the Sails $(o)(S)$(), and furl them fully $(o)(R)$() to drift to a Stop.$(br)    Mind that your Ship responds not as a Nag to the Whip – adjustments to the Sails need Moments to effect. Note too that a Ship alters course with some Reluctance – and the larger the Vessel, the wider her Turns. The wise Pilot is patient.$(br)    If your Craft is fitted with Oars, you may engage them by directing the Crew to row $(o)(hold W)$() – adding their Strength to the Wind, or maneuvering by Oar alone for finer control.$(p)
